text:
Elliot Price: hey docs folks — starting a thread to map the onboarding checklist steps -> canonical docs pages. trying to get to a single source of truth we can link from Console step drawer + quickstarts. dropping initial draft below. pls reply w gaps / bad links / missing how-tos.

Elliot Price: Draft mapping (Hosted API MVP):
1) Create API key -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/console/api-keys (needs troubleshooting for 401/403)
2) Set env var + first request -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/quickstart (language switcher)
3) Enable streaming -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/streaming
4) Add retries/timeouts -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/retries-and-timeouts
5) Understand rate limits + 429 handling -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/platform/rate-limits
6) View usage dashboard -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/console/usage
7) Set quotas/budgets -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/console/quotas-and-budgets
8) Pin model version -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/models/versioning
9) Configure fallback policy -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/fallbacks
10) Add observability hooks (request_id, tracing) -> https://docs.redwoodinference.com/guides/observability

Elliot Price: Known weak spots already: (a) streaming disconnect guidance is thin, (b) 429 page exists but doesn’t show concrete backoff examples per SDK, (c) usage dashboard lag / “why don’t I see tokens yet?” isn’t covered.

Wei Chen: thx. quickstart link is fine but it currently stops right after “hello world” and doesn’t mention production-safe defaults. we should add callouts + a section that mirrors the checklist order (at least for steps 3–7). I can take that for the quickstart update.

Wei Chen: also, model versioning page is a little buried under /models. might want a short alias under /guides/model-pinning so checklist deep link is more obvious.

Jean-Paul Laurent: for Console step drawer copy, we should avoid linking 3 diff pages for “first request” depending on language. can we keep quickstart as canonical and then have language-specific snippets inside it? (or deep links w anchors like #python / #typescript)

Elliot Price: +1 anchors. we can do /quickstart#python etc. I’ll check with docs-site config.

Priya Shah: flagging real support pain points:
- “401 invalid api key” is usually wrong env var name OR copied key includes whitespace. doc should literally show `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` + “no quotes” note.
- 429 confusion: customers think it’s an outage. we need “429 == quota/rate limit, not server error” + “read response headers” guidance.
- streaming: folks see half a response then disconnect and assume model is broken. usually their client/proxy times out idle connections.

Priya Shah: I can paste common macro text if helpful.

Elliot Price: yes please, paste macro text. we’ll convert to “Troubleshooting” callouts.

Sabrina James: mapping looks right, but the retries/timeouts guide is currently generic and only has python examples. we’ll need TS + Go parity if it’s a checklist step. can we track as a docs task? (I can help w TS snippet.)

Ibrahim Khan: streaming disconnects: we should document reconnection strategy and what is/isn’t safe to retry.
- safe: retry on connection drop *before* receiving any tokens
- after partial tokens: depends on idempotency / you can’t “resume” generation unless you re-send prompt with a stop condition etc.
- server sends `x-request-id` and `x-redwood-attempt` headers (we should verify exact header names) -> clients should log them

Ibrahim Khan: we also need to explicitly mention read timeout / keepalive. a bunch of users behind Cloudflare have 100s timeouts.

Kenji Nakamura: from UX side: checklist step drawer can only show ~2–3 links max before it feels noisy. ideally 1 canonical doc per step + maybe 1 “troubleshooting” anchor. so if streaming guide is missing disconnect section, best to add it there vs creating a new page.

Elliot Price: makes sense. proposal:
- streaming guide becomes canonical for step 3 + add section “Common disconnects + how to handle” w SDK patterns + infra notes
- rate limits page becomes canonical for step 5 + add “Handling 429s” section w copy/paste snippets per SDK
- usage page add “Data freshness + dashboard lag” FAQ

Wei Chen: +1. also add explicit “what counts as success” language: first 2xx response vs first streamed token. aligns w checklist acceptance criteria.

Elliot Price: yup. we’ll keep it user-facing: “You’ll see a 200 response / tokens streamed” rather than event names.

Priya Shah: macro text (current):
“429 indicates your org hit a rate limit or quota. Recommended: implement exponential backoff w jitter for retries, and check your limits in Console > Quotas. If this started right after go-live, you likely need a higher burst limit or dedicated capacity. Please share your org id + approx QPS + model.”

Priya Shah: also common headers we ask for: request id + timestamp + region.

Sabrina James: I can draft TS snippet for 429 backoff using our SDK helper once the interface is final. for now I’ll do a plain example.

Ibrahim Khan: pls also call out: don’t retry non-idempotent requests blindly. For chat completions it’s usually fine if you set an idempotency key per user action.

Elliot Price: good point — where do we want idempotency content to live? retries guide or a separate page?

Wei Chen: I’d keep it in retries/timeouts guide under “Idempotency keys” section. checklist step 4 can link there.

Kenji Nakamura: +1 keep it consolidated.

Elliot Price: ok action items:
- Elliot: update mapping doc + propose redirects/aliases; add TODO list for missing sections
- Wei: update quickstart to mirror checklist (3–7) w anchors (#python/#ts/#go)
- Sabrina: TS snippet support (429 + retry defaults) once doc structure is set
- Ibrahim: draft streaming disconnect guidance (safe retry rules + keepalive/timeouts)
- Priya: share any other macros esp “usage dashboard lag”

Elliot Price: Gaps list (tracking):
1) Streaming guide missing disconnect + reconnect patterns (SDK parity)
2) Rate limits doc missing concrete 429 handling examples + “not an outage” messaging
3) Usage dashboard doc missing freshness/lag FAQ
4) Retries/timeouts doc missing TS/Go + idempotency guidance

Wei Chen: :thumbsup: I’ll start on quickstart today and will ping for review.

Priya Shah: usage lag macro: “Usage dashboard can lag by up to ~15 minutes depending on region and aggregation window. Token counts are still metered in real time for billing/quota enforcement. If you don’t see usage after 30 minutes, share request ids and we’ll investigate.”

Elliot Price: perfect. will incorporate.

Sabrina James: one more: we should ensure every page linked from checklist has a “Last updated” footer + minimal jargon. checklist users are brand new.

Elliot Price: agreed. I’ll add a sweep for tone/verbosity once content lands.

Elliot Price: I’m going to turn this mapping into a table doc + link it in the checklist template + console spec. will post draft for async comments.

Wei Chen: pls include anchor links in the table so Console deep links land in the right section.

Elliot Price: will do.
